title: Interviewer & Observer Cheatsheet + Offer Handoff
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight operational reference for interviewers, observers, and hiring coordinators that ties together the interview day conduct expectations, observer note priorities, immediate post-interview handoff, and the offer-acceptance contingency flows. Keep this open in the final interview loop and during scheduling/offer conversations.

Scope and usage notes (quick):
- Primary audience: interviewers (ICs/managers), interview observers (hiring committee members), recruiting coordinators, and hiring managers.
- Use in final-stage interviews and any candidate-facing loop where multiple stakeholders will weigh in.
- Not a rubric. This complements the rubric (see linked Confluence). Focus is logistics + signal prioritization + candidate experience.

Top-of-mind principles (TL;DR):
- Candidates should leave knowing next steps and an approximate calendar.
- Observers capture 3 signals: competency, collaboration/hypotheses, and fit risks. Keep notes short.
- Handoffs must happen within 24 hours of last interview (recruiter + hiring manager).
- Offer contingencies (declines, relocation, visa, counteroffers) are triaged into the recruiter + people-ops playbook within 48 hours.

Before the interview (interviewer checklist):
- Review candidate resume + past interview notes 15–30 minutes before.
- Confirm the mission context: what problem will this hire solve in the first 6 months?
- Prepare 2 core questions (one technical/role-specific, one behavior/collaboration).
- Avoid open-ended system design without clear timebox; pick scoped prompts.
- Bring deliberate acceptance criteria: what would make you recommend hire / no-hire / needs-more-evidence?
- Silent policy: if you expect a no-hire because of skill gap, prepare an explicit example during the conversation.

During the interview (interviewer conduct):
- Start with framing (5 min): role context, interview goal, and timeboxing.
- Use paired problem solving for 20–35 minute technical segments: let candidate talk, ask clarifying Qs, surface trade-offs.
- Signal to candidate if you’re looking for a specific depth (e.g., “I’m probing system thinking vs micro-optimization”).
- Avoid surprising assessment criteria at the end — be explicit about strengths and missing signals.
- Capture two short notes mid-interview (mental bookmarks): one good example, one gap or ambiguity.

Observer cheatsheet (what to capture, in order of priority):
1) Summary verdict (one-line): hire / lean-hire / neutral / lean-no / no-hire. Keep it short.
2) Top evidence (2 bullets): concrete candidate actions or answers that justify the verdict. Link to timecodes if recorded.
3) Risk signals (2 bullets): collaboration red-flags, unclear ownership, misalignment on scope.
4) Follow-ups / open questions: one-line list for additional probe in next round or reference check.
5) Candidate experience notes: tone, punctuality, questions asked, enthusiasm level (scale 1–5).

Post-interview immediate actions (first 24 hours):
- Interviewers: submit short written feedback in the interview form within 12 hours. Use the one-line verdict + 2 evidence bullets format.
- Hiring manager: review consolidated feedback within 24 hours, call the recruiter if multiple strong candidates.
- Recruiter: confirm candidate availability for next steps and tentatively block time for calendar windows.

Offer handoff checklist (recruiter + hiring manager):
- Within 24 hours: hiring manager confirms compensation band and target start date range.
- Recruiter drafts offer summary (base, equity, sign-on if applicable, benefits summary, start window).
- People-ops (if flagged): confirm relocation support, visa sponsorship, or special accommodations.
- Check: any outstanding background checks or reference checks needed prior to verbal offer? If yes, initiate immediately.
- Candidate communication: recruiter to provide verbal timeline for formal offer (goal: verbal within 48–72 hours of final interview).

Contingency flows (common edges):
1) Candidate declines verbal offer: recruiter debriefs within 6 hours, asks for primary reason and whether counter-proposal would help. Escalate to hiring manager and people-ops as needed.
2) Visa/relocation delay: if candidate needs >60 days, hiring manager + people-ops evaluate criticality vs benching. Consider contract/temporary start options.
3) Competing counteroffer from current employer: recruiter offers retention/mission talking points, schedules hiring manager call within 24 hours.
4) Reference or background flags: people-ops + hiring manager triage and request clarifying references; document decisions in candidate’s file.

Day-0 (pre-start) rapid checklist — recruiter + hiring manager responsibilities: 
- Recruiter: confirm signed offer received, send welcome packet, assign buddy, request any paperwork (tax, IDs).
- Hiring manager: schedule first-week 1:1s, confirm equipment plan, invite to core team channels, prepare a 30-minute welcome meeting and a 2-hour orientation with product/tech context.
- IT/Facilities: gear requested and delivery ETA (confirm before candidate signs).
- People-ops: confirm benefits enrollment timeline and initial payroll info.

First-week synchronous plan (sample agenda to share w/manager):
Day 1: welcome meeting (30 min), team intro (60 min), orientation/walkthrough (90 min), buddy lunch.
Day 2: role onboarding deep dive (90 min), first small task assigned.
Day 3: cross-team meetups (VCs/PM/infra), setup/credentials review.
Day 4: start contribution sprint (clear, scoped ticket).
Day 5: end-week sync + feedback loop (30 min).

Templates (short)
- Interviewer note template (one line verdict + 2 bullets):
  Verdict: lean-hire
  Evidence: (1) implemented a caching proof-of-concept during live whiteboard; (2) clearly articulated trade-offs and latency/cost implications.
  Risk: limited infra debugging experience beyond Python.
  Follow-up: Ask for code sample or pair debugging session.

- Recruiter verbal-offer script (short bullets):
  1) Thanks + congratulations. We’d like to extend a verbal offer today for X role (level) with base $$$, equity Y, sign-on Z.
  2) Confirm start window and relocation needs.
  3) We’ll email formal offer within 24–48 hours. Expect benefits docs and next steps for background check.

Unresolved / discussion items (notes to self):
- Should observers be required to submit a minimum note length? (currently not — ops friction vs signal completeness).
- Investigate simple timecode links for recorded loops (privacy/compliance gating).
- Local compensation exceptions: clarify when hiring manager can commit pre-offer.

Quick links and references: (lift to Confluence where finalized)
- Interview rubric (detailed): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HR/Interviewer+Framework
- Hiring coordinator checklist (detailed): JIRA-7812
- Offer templates (legal-approved): /docs/legal/offer-templates (internal)

Notes to readers:
- This doc is deliberately terse — keep it visible on interview days and share with new interviewers as part of short shadowing.
- If you update this file, add your name and date in the short changelog at the top.

Changelog:
- 2025-10-15 Asha Patel: initial draft with observer template and offer flow.
- 2025-11-02 Priya Rao: added contingency flows and day-0 checklist.
